description: Fit a video to a target duration and/or aspect ratio.

argv.description: raw CLI arguments (non-canonical compatibility path; when present every other key is ignored)

audio_stream.description: which audio stream of the input to keep, 0-based in file order (probe.py lists them under audio_streams) -- matters on a multi-track input (dubbed languages, M&E stems); default 0, the first track, same as leaving it unset always did

codec.description: video encoder for the re-encode: h264 (x264, the default for SDR), hevc (x265, the default for HDR), av1 (SVT-AV1 or libaom), prores (422 HQ, needs a .mov/.mkv output); HDR sources keep their colour on hevc/av1/prores

dry_run.description: print the ffmpeg commands that would run, run nothing

fade_in.description: fade the picture and the sound in from black over this many seconds at the start

fade_out.description: fade the picture and the sound out to black over this many seconds at the end

fast.description: preview quality: x264 preset veryfast (overrides --preset) for quick iterations

fit.description: the fit mode, how to reach the aspect: pad (letterbox), crop, or blur -- the whole picture centred on a blurred, darkened copy of itself filling the rest (the phone-editor vertical, 1.14). The darkening is applied to SDR sources only: on an HDR source the background is blurred but left at its own levels, since an eq on PQ/HLG code values is not a -15%% perceptual dim

flip.description: mirror the picture horizontally (h) or vertically (v)

fps.description: force a constant output frame rate (recommended for VFR sources)

from_center.description: with --method trim, keep the middle instead of the start

height.description: output height in px, 1..16384 (default: keep source height or the height implied by the aspect); with --width also given, both are used directly

hw.description: encode on the GPU with Apple VideoToolbox (h264/hevc/prores; Apple Silicon only): several times faster, larger files at the same quality; falls back to the CPU encoder, reported, where it cannot apply

json_brief.description: like --json but trimmed: status, output, dry_run, verified, a compact summary of the output probe, this tool's own keys, and the command count instead of the command lines (failures print the full failure document, unchanged)

method.description: how to reach the duration (small retimes default to speed; larger changes need an explicit choice)

no_hw.description: encode on the CPU (x264/x265/SVT-AV1/prores_ks) even when $FFMPEG_SKILL_HW=1

overwrite.description: allow replacing an existing output (refused without it)

pad_blur.description: blur radius in pixels for --pad-fill blur (default 20)

pad_color.description: pad colour, e.g. black, white, 0x101010 (default black)

pad_fill.description: what fills the letterbox/pillarbox bars under --fit pad: a solid --pad-color (default) or a blurred, scaled-up copy of the frame

plan.description: write the dry run as a plan (inputs fingerprinted, commands, expected output, verify steps) that render.py FILE executes later; implies --dry-run

quality.description: encoder quality on the CRF scale (default 18; lower = better; 18 visually lossless for x264/x265, up to 63 for av1); ignored by prores

rotate.description: rotate the picture clockwise by this angle in degrees

smooth.description: slow-motion quality: blend (frame blending) or interpolate (motion-compensated, slow but fluid). default none = duplicate frames

timeout.description: kill an ffmpeg run past this many seconds, kind=timeout (default 1800; 0 = no limit)

width.description: output width in px, 1..16384 (default: keep source width or the width implied by the aspect); with --height also given, both are used directly

name: fit
